key_insight: A reinforcement-learning plus CGCNN pipeline can generate and rank novel metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for photocatalysis by optimizing multiple practical objectives at once.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a computational design workflow for screening industrially relevant porous materials with constraints such as stability, cost, sustainability, and adsorption performance.
method: Generated 60,000 novel MOFs with reinforcement learning.
Used a predictor funnel to prune candidates to 10,986 for efficient evaluation.
Built a multi-objective fitness function from CGCNN-predicted properties and application-specific criteria.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two top MOFs that passed synthesis criteria, including one Cr-based design with a photocatalyst score 230% above the control and a Zn-based design that outperformed the best control across relevant metrics.
watch_item: Results depend on model predictions and the chosen fitness function, so experimental validation is still needed before deployment.
paper_title: Machine Learning for Designing Undesignable Metal-Organic Frameworks
